key_insight: A lubrication-based model links evaporation, curvature, and interfacial forces to thinning and instability of volatile films on heated vertical cylinders.
engineering_relevance: The findings could guide thermal management, evaporative cooling, and heat-exchanger designs that rely on stable liquid-film coverage.
method: Model nonlinear film evolution with gravity, surface tension, van der Waals forces, and pressure-dependent evaporation.
Analyze linear stability for uniform and spatially nonuniform films, using finite elements for the latter.
Numerically simulate liquid–vapor interface evolution and droplet dynamics.
evidence_signal: Stability analysis and simulations indicate that evaporation accelerates thinning, condensation promotes thickening, and the modeled van der Waals forces prevent ultra-thin-film rupture.
watch_item: The abstract reports no experimental validation; predictions depend on thin-film assumptions and the chosen evaporation and intermolecular-force laws.
paper_title: Dynamics and stability of volatile thin liquid films on a heated vertical cylinder
